p.i: Cur Gultus illi tristior? Cur nunc iubet
Quid ille quæso, nunc timet: discrimina
Qui rebus aduersis animum nil territum
Quid ergo nunc illum angit? haud quisquam parat
Mouere bellum. Nam licet terra incolas
Rebus suis sedes, Gɛ auri possidens
Vita, Gɛ nocere Gilli cauentem sedulo,
Se iunxit Gltro, cuncta domi sunt prospera,
Ornata fugit rixas, suo studens Giro
Qua peperit annis, quo nihil suauius
Sol cernit Gsquam, nec senium potentius
Leuare radia Gɛ graues Gita moras:
Non Gizit Gllus orbe toto, nec suo
Fauore quem magis Superum tegat pater.

page.notes: Several words in the verse are doubtful, notably the Gothic-looking forms "Gultus", "Gsque", "Gerentur", "Gizit", "Gllus", "Gita" and "Gltro", which I could not read with certainty and have transcribed as they appear. The page has no printed page number or running head. The "Facunda" at lower right is a catchword for the next page.
